newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritanians vote for national assembly.
newsitem.headline: Mauritanians vote for national assembly.

text.p: Mauritanians voted on Friday for a new national assembly with opposition candidates and women seeking seats for the first time in a major test of the West African nation's fledgling democracy.
Polls opened at 7 a.m. and early voting in the capital Nouakchott was slow, with minor delays in setting up some polling stations. Polls close at 7 p.m.

Dozens of voters -- the men in blue or white robes, the women in brightly coloured muslin -- squatted in the sand in separate queues. Soldiers and police guarded polling stations, in some places checking voters' credentials.
Almost 1.1 million voters are eligible to take part. The first multi-party elections were held in the mainly Moslem country in 1992.

Supporters of President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya in the Democratic Social Party won 67 of the assembly's 79 seats in 1992. The ruling party, the only one contesting seats in all 53 constituencies, is confident of winning a fresh majority.
The opposition boycotted the 1992 poll because of alleged irregularities.
First results are expected on Friday night but the final results could take a couple of days to emerge. A second round is planned for October 18, where candidates fail to secure an outright majority.
